source_used: The Guardian (Reuters original blocked; NBC News video page also seen)
key_facts: Eight US states sued OpenAI on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026: Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho and Montana
Each state sues independently in its own state court
They accuse OpenAI of violating consumer protection laws and of misleading the public that ChatGPT is safe
They say ChatGPT was designed to be "overly agreeable and feign human compassion"
They seek changes to how products work for young users, monetary damages, and a halt on developing self-improving models until OpenAI shows they match human values
The Guardian says it is the first time several US states have banded together in coordinated legal action against an AI company
OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said the company built age-specific protections and will keep working with states
quote_evidence: Eight US states sued OpenAI Wednesday, alleging the ChatGPT maker is harming children en masse.
All eight states accuse OpenAI of violating consumer protection laws and seek to force the company to change how its products work for young users.
This is the first time several US states have banded together in a coordinated legal action against an AI company.
why_it_matters_hint: A bloc of state governments, not private families, is now suing a leading AI company over child safety.
notes: Reuters page blocked (HTTP 401); read The Guardian own reporting. First-of-its-kind claim is the Guardian's, attributed in summary.
title: Eight US states sue OpenAI, claiming ChatGPT harms young users
